assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the subsequent experimental realisation of ion-based gates, entanglement and small processors form the intellectual foundation of hardware quantum computing, and the same ideas seeded analogue quantum simulation with cold atoms. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all high, and the field has grown into industrial programmes.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the decisive theorists for the 1995 gate proposal. Blatt is a leading experimentalist who demonstrated the central operations in Innsbruck; the 2012 prize to Wineland (with Haroche) already recognised ion control and a fair three-way split needs care about how Blatt's role differs from Wineland's and Monroe's. Wineland and Monroe are not in the credited names, so the supplied credit is a partial map.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of independent confirmation across many ion and atom laboratories. The platform is stable and still advancing, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for manipulating individual quantum systems may be argued to dilute novelty.
The candidate bundles quantum-computing foundations with ultracold-atom simulation; the parts may deserve different recognition.
Whether Blatt or other experimenters outside the credited names should complete the configuration is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between a single microwave photon and a superconducting artificial atom routine, and it is the architecture behind transmon qubits, dispersive readout and most current superconducting processors. The impact on quantum technology and on microwave quantum optics is large and clearly stated. I note my own field and institutional closeness to this area and have weighed it conservatively.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the experimental demonstration (Wallraff et al.) are tightly linked. Schoelkopf and Wallraff are the experimental leaders, and Girvin or Blais the theory anchors. Only three can be chosen from four credited names, and the choice between Girvin and Blais is a genuine allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Replicated and extended in many groups for two decades. However, the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, so near-term recognition of the same platform could be seen as premature or as redundant by colleagues.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may argue for waiting.
Allocation among Schoelkopf, Wallraff, Girvin and Blais, and the role of Devoret's group in the circuit-QED lineage, is not settled by the supplied credit.
My Chalmers and WACQT connections to this community call for a cautious reading of my own preference.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 turned quantum mechanics into a cryptographic resource with security grounded in physical law, and they created the field of quantum communication. The ideas are original, simple and have lasting influence across physics and information science, with commercial and satellite implementations.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84, and Ekert introduced the entanglement-based protocol that links the idea to Bell tests. The three-name configuration is natural and fits the credited names. Other contributors to security proofs (for example Mayers, Lo-Chau, Shor-Preskill) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Roughly forty years of development with extensive experimental confirmation of protocols, though practical security rests on implementation details. The 2022 prize touched entanglement and quantum information, so timing relative to that prize needs thought.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests.
Whether the physics content rather than the information-theoretic content is the right Nobel scope is open.
Security proofs and practical device loopholes are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model and was a landmark in instrumentation, data analysis and collaboration. Importance and clarity are very high, and the 2013 prize recognised only the theoretical prediction.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty because the discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands. Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee are the founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS proposals, but the physics discovery credit also involves analysis and spokesperson roles that the supplied names do not capture. The rules limit the prize to three people and no organisation.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by two independent experiments and later coupling measurements, so the result is mature. The interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Individual credit in very large collaborations is not objectively resolvable from the supplied names.
Whether leaders of the proposals, rather than discovery-era spokespeople, are appropriate is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological classification, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe wells, opened the field of topological insulators and has shaped condensed-matter research and materials discovery. The concept is original and its influence is wide.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the decisive theorists for the Z2 insulator in graphene and the classification. Molenkamp led the HgTe experiment with the Zhang-theory prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang), so Shoucheng Zhang's absence from the credited names and his death complicate a fair configuration. The three listed names form a workable but incomplete set.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations, notably ARPES and transport on three-dimensional topological insulators. The 2016 prize for topological phases covers adjacent ground, so timeliness is arguable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.
Credit for the HgTe prediction and for three-dimensional topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hasan) is not fully represented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, giving quantum simulation of many-body physics such as the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site resolved imaging. The scientific impact is considerable and the platform is general.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied key theory proposals (with Jaksch and others), Bloch and Greiner carried out landmark experiments, and Esslinger's group made parallel contributions. With a four-name credit and a limit of three, the choice excludes Esslinger and others, and Greiner and Bloch's Mott transition work builds on Hänsch and Greiner's earlier lineage and on the 2001 BEC prize.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories and increasingly a source of quantitative results, though the claim of broad advantage for solving open problems is still developing.
uncertainties: Substantial overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with candidate B021 on Zoller and cold-atom foundations.
Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations of record accuracy are original and have clear metrological impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye's group achieved the leading performance, so a two-person configuration is clear. Other clock groups (for example Lemke, Ludlow, Schiller, Takamoto) and the contribution of the frequency comb prize of 2005 are relevant context.
assessment.maturity: Multiple laboratories have confirmed the performance, and the field is mature, though a formal redefinition of the second has not happened yet.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2005 recognition of frequency-comb spectroscopy and 2012 recognition of ion clocks.
Jun Ye also appears in other candidate groupings, such as the thorium clock.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought mechanical resonators to the quantum ground state and enabled radiation-pressure sideband cooling, squeezing and entanglement of macroscopic motion. This links closely to the circuit-based macroscopic quantum physics that I know well, and its sensing and transduction applications are growing.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg led optical optomechanics, and Cleland demonstrated quantum control of a mechanical resonator coupled to a superconducting qubit, so the three names cover separate but connected achievements. Others (such as Painter, Schwab, Lehnert, Teufel) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Ground-state cooling and quantum control have been reproduced in several platforms, but the leading applications, such as quantum transduction, are still maturing; the prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits partly overlaps conceptually.
Optical and electromechanical branches may need different recognition, and the credit boundary between them is disputed.
